claude_proposed_widenings.name: ClassFeatureActivationCost { kind: "action" }
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The Temporary Hit Points sub-feature costs a Magic action (i.e., the standard Action to cast a spell or use a magic feature). The current ClassFeatureActivationCost only allows 'free' and 'bonus_action'. 'action' is a distinct, common activation cost needed here.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "As a Magic action, you can give yourself a number of Temporary Hit Points..."

claude_proposed_widenings.name: grant_temp_hp
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The effect grants Temporary Hit Points, which are mechanically distinct from regular healing (heal_hp). Temporary HP form a separate HP buffer, don't stack, and are not subject to the same interactions as real HP recovery. The v4 taxonomy has 'heal' but not 'grant_temp_hp'. ClassFeatureEffect has HealHpEffect but that covers actual HP restoration.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "you can give yourself a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to 1d8 plus your Wisdom modifier"

claude_proposed_widenings.name: UseCountCap { kind: "ability_score_derived"; ability: Ability; minimum: number }
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The use count scales with Wisdom modifier (minimum 1), not a fixed number or a level-threshold schedule. UseCountCap currently supports 'fixed' and 'threshold_tiers'. An ability-score-derived use count is a distinct cap shape needed for several class features.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "You can use this action a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once)"

claude_proposed_widenings.name: DiceExpr flat: { kind: "ability_modifier"; ability: Ability } | number
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The temp HP amount is 1d8 + Wisdom modifier. DiceExpr.flat is currently a static number. An ability modifier addend is a distinct shape needed to honestly encode the heal/temp-HP amount here.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "Temporary Hit Points equal to 1d8 plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1)"

claude_proposed_widenings.name: ClassFeatureMechanics family: "passive_rest_trigger"
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The Decrease Exhaustion sub-feature has no activation cost, no use count, and no reset cadence — it fires automatically whenever a Short Rest ends. There is no existing ClassFeatureMechanics family that can honestly model a passive rest-triggered effect. A 'passive_rest_trigger' family (or equivalent) is needed, pairing a RestKind trigger with an effect (here: reduce exhaustion by 1).
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "Whenever you finish a Short Rest, your Exhaustion level, if any, decreases by 1."

claude_proposed_widenings.name: reduce_exhaustion (or: extend remove_condition to cover exhaustion levels)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Decreasing an exhaustion level by 1 is a partial-reduction effect distinct from 'remove_condition' (which would clear it entirely). Exhaustion is not in the current Condition type either. v4 has 'remove_condition' but exhaustion level decrement is a graded operation. This may be a new atom or a typed extension of remove_condition with a 'levels' field.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "your Exhaustion level, if any, decreases by 1"
